traits.leaf_arrangement.note: APweb, Malvales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): leaves spiral; opposite leaves only in Thymelaeaceae (often) and Cistaceae.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): leaves spiral at order level; two-ranked in Muntingiaceae, some Sphaerosepalaceae and Diegodendron. 'sometimes' distichous also covers two-ranked Malvaceae (Grewioideae, Tilioideae), a weighting inferred.

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): blades mostly simple (Thymelaeaceae entire, Neuradaceae toothed to pinnatifid); palmately compound leaves only in part of Malvaceae (Bombacoideae).

traits.division_pattern.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): venation palmate or from the blade base; Cochlospermum palmately lobed; compound Malvaceae leaves are palmate.

traits.rosette.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): mostly trees and shrubs with leafy stems; no rosette plants described.

traits.life_span.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): mostly trees and shrubs; annuals in Neuradaceae and some herbaceous Thymelaeaceae and Malvaceae.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): flowers regular across the order; monosymmetry only in Cochlospermum (weak) and oblique in Grielum.

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): the few zygomorphic flowers are weakly or obliquely so, with no lipped or pea plan.

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): corolla of free, often contorted petals that open out; funnel-like corollas (Hibiscus and kin) added as 'sometimes', inferred.

traits.hypanthium.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): a long hypanthium is a mark of Thymelaeaceae; not described for the other families.

traits.ovary_position.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): inferior ovaries only in Cytinaceae, Neuradaceae (more or less) and some Muntingiaceae.

traits.stamens.note: APweb, Malvales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): stamens usually numerous. Replaces the rosid 5-10 value, which is wrong for this order.

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): Bixaceae 2-5, Cytinaceae 3-14, Muntingiaceae 5(-7), Neuradaceae about 10. Typical 5 weighted by Malvaceae, which states its own typical 5.

traits.fruit_type.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): capsules in Cochlospermum, Cistaceae and most Malvaceae; nut-like winged fruits in Dipterocarpaceae (state their own); fleshy in Cytinaceae and Sphaerosepalaceae.

traits.sexual_system.note: APweb, Malvales page (read 2026-10-16): Thymelaeaceae mostly perfect, some dioecious or monoecious; Cytinaceae unisexual. Rest bisexual.
